report.executive_summary: Judged against the client policy — quality index at least 80, at most five raw defects, then lowest energy on the shared acceptance run — all four candidates clear both gates, and P2 wins the energy ranking decisively at 12 kWh per run. The nearest rival, P3, trails by 40 kWh; P1 trails by 44 kWh and P4 by 46 kWh on the same fixed flow and head duty. P2 also carries the strongest quality index (97) with a single recorded defect. P4 alone reports zero defects, but on the supplied basis that distinction does not offset its energy penalty. Cost, delivery and field reliability remain unverified and are excluded from this ranking.

recommendation.rationale: P2 is the lowest-energy qualifying candidate at 12 kWh, clears both gates with quality 97 and one defect, and beats every rival by 40+ kWh on an identical test basis. P4's zero-defect record is the best reliability signal but carries a 46 kWh penalty with no policy weight attached. No verified fact supports overriding the energy rule.

sections.body: The trusted table lists four anonymous pump modules. Every candidate satisfies the quality floor: P2 at 97, P1 at 84, P4 at 81 and P3 at exactly 80. Every candidate also sits inside the defect ceiling of five: P4 reports zero, P2 one, P3 three and P1 four raw defects. Qualification is therefore unanimous, and the decision reduces entirely to measured energy on the common acceptance run, where each module serves the same fixed flow and head duty. The verified order is P2 at 12 kWh, P3 at 52, P1 at 56 and P4 at 58. No candidate is disqualified, and reject_all does not apply.
sections.heading: Ranking and Qualification of the Four Candidates

sections.body: Quality separation is real but secondary under the stated policy. P2 leads with 97, a seventeen-point margin over P3's floor-level 80, which qualifies with no headroom. P4's 81 clears the floor narrowly while posting the field's only zero-defect record, a materially stronger reliability signal than P2's single defect. P1 combines 84 quality with four defects, the weakest qualifying defect position. They matter only if the client applies weighting beyond the three published criteria. On the basis supplied, they change no ranking: quality and defects act only as gates; energy alone orders the qualified field.
sections.heading: Quality and Defect Profiles Across the Field

sections.body: Because the test basis is identical for every module — same output, same load, same acceptance run — the energy column is directly comparable and decides the outcome. P2 consumes 12 kWh, roughly a fifth of P4's 58 kWh and of P1's 56 kWh; P3's 52 kWh sits 40 kWh above the winner. The gaps to the winner are 40 kWh (P3), 44 kWh (P1) and 46 kWh (P4), each far larger than any plausible measurement nuance in a single run. Even if energy estimates carried meaningful uncertainty, a 40-plus-kWh spread would be robust. On the supplied facts, P2's energy advantage is unambiguous.
sections.heading: Lowest-Energy Comparison on the Common Basis

sections.body: P4 deserves separate mention: it is the only module with zero raw defects, and if the client later adopts a defect-weighted override, P4 — not P3 or P1 — would be its natural challenger. That scenario is hypothetical; no such rule appears in the supplied policy, so P4 remains the last-ranked qualified module at 58 kWh. Open questions: unit cost, delivery schedule, maintenance burden and field reliability are all unverified; no weighting beyond quality, defects and energy is supplied. Verification should recompute the gate arithmetic, confirm energy figures against the trusted table, and log any client clarification before award.
